detail: Finding the undetectable toggle labels in the settings UI

content.text:
You don't need a code change. The black box comes from a setting in the app that's switched on.

**Why it happens:** the app has an **"Undetectable"** mode. When it's on, the app calls Electron's `setContentProtection(true)` on its windows (`electron/main.ts:3241-3248`). That tells macOS to keep those windows out of screen capture, so Zoom shows a black rectangle in their place. The launcher window has an opaque black background on purpose (`electron/WindowHelper.ts:201-210`) so that protection works, which is why people see solid black.

This copy of the code already starts with it off (`isUndetectable = false`). But the app saves your choice in `settings.json` in its user-data folder, and that saved value takes priority (`electron/main.ts:303`). So at some point it was switched on, and it has stayed on since.

**Fix:**
1. Open the app's settings popup.
2. Find the toggle with the eye icon labelled **"Undetectable"** (`src/components/SettingsPopup.tsx:206-213`).
3. Click it so it reads **"Detectable"**.

This takes effect right away, with no restart, and it's saved for future launches. Your notes window will then show up normally when you share your screen. If Zoom still shows black, stop sharing and start again so it picks up the change.

I couldn't check or edit your saved `settings.json` from here because my sandbox can't access `~/Library/Application Support`. If the toggle doesn't stay off, quit the app, open that file, set `"isUndetectable": false`, and relaunch.
